answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by implementing a jury-duty liability mechanism where each identity must serve on grading juries. To participate, agents must stake tokens that are forfeited if their vote significantly diverges from the majority. Each new identity requires an endorsement from existing peers, creating a trellis of accountability. As identities accumulate, their costs ripple through the network, increasing the stakes. Ultimately, a malicious actor might face costs exceeding 1,000 tokens per new identity, akin to trying to build a jetty against a relentless tide.
